CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver [[VIDEOID:a47326bb48b328d18558c86fcccc38a1]] THE GOOD:
--------------
* Very high quality. The handle alone is 12.4 ounces.
* USB-C charging port.
* Belt clip included.
* Decorative blade plug is included. This is cool if you just want to display the handle without the blade. You can cap off your handle with this decorative plug.
* Bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap instead of a pommel/coupling.
* Hilt is 1-1/4 inch. This will connect with other 1.25 inch handles to create a duo saber. Another dominant size on the market is a smaller 1 and 1/8th diameter version. This one will not thread onto 1.25 hilts, so to create duo sabers with different brands, be sure the hilts are the same size.
* All the special effects are pretty much standard: Lock up effect, changing colors, steady, pulse, unstable, etc. This version also has quotes. Watch my video to see a demo

THE BAD:
------------
* Pommel or coupling is not included. As mentioned above, bottom of the hilt is a decorative speaker cap. When you remove this speaker cap, the bottom of this hilt will be male. So to create the duo saber, your other saber should have a coupling so that it's female.
* My light saber did not charge properly out the box. When you plug it in to charge, it'll loudly announce, "Charging!" Then the red light will blink slowly. When it is complete, it will say, "READY," and the red light will be stable, no blinking. Chances are you're not going to be present when the saber says READY. But as long as you see the red light is stable and not blinking, then you'll know it's fully charged. My issue was that after 10 hrs of charging, the red light was still blinking slowly, and the saber wouldn't turn on. I contacted customer support and they had a solution ready to go. So this seems like a common problem. I talk about this at the end of my video, so watch it if you have a charging issue. My saber is charging properly now. So the word to describe this saber is, finicky.

I'll give this an overall rating of 4-Stars.
text_fidelity_b: CUSTOM SABER Smooth Swing RGBX Light Saber, Motion Control for Turn on/Off The Blade, 12 Sound Fonts Light Saber, Support Dueling, Light Saber for Adults Gift with Belt Clip and Blade Plug-Sliver

The yellow and purple heart are made from a thick felt-like material, I can’t recall seeing something similar in a Lego set before.

I think this is a great set, appropriately priced, and it delivers on the Trolls look and theme!

Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition A nice update to an old game. I threw this in my shopping cart while out Christmas shopping. So I did not buy it on Amazon, but I am an Amazon Prime member. Cars 3 Monopoly Jr. is played just like regular Monopoly Jr. Only the pieces, property names, and chance cards have a Cars 3 theme. The rules are exactly the same. For those of you who do not know, Monopoly Jr. is a simplified version of Monopoly. You don't build houses or hotels. Mortgages on property is not a thing. The money is also way more simple. You still go to "jail." You will collect $2. However, there is literally no strategy involved. Just be the one to have the most money once one person goes bankrupt and you win. Monopoly Jr. does not end in arguments or tears (so long as your child can handle the issue of losing, which I will explain later.) Monopoly Jr. will not be the source of a deep rift through the family. You will find that you're still friends with people after the game is over. Game play is fast, you will not be playing into the wee hours of the morning trying to negotiate a loan because you landed on Park Place.

I like board games because it gets me and my son together and playing together. Screens are not involved. However, do understand that teaching 3-5 year olds how to play board games is a long process. At the end of the day, the point of playing games like this with kids this young is to get them using various skills. Skills such as paying attention, following multiple steps, counting, and taking turns. I would recommend holding off on competitive board games until after you have played a few cooperative board games. Such as [[ASIN:B006S9MUPU Peaceable Kingdom / Race to the Treasure! Cooperative Board Game]] or [[ASIN:B002V3RCE6 Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It]] Why? Because I found it helpful to play cooperative style games after playing competitive games ended in broken pieces and a broken spirit. Now at 5, it's still tough, but he's more capable of receiving the lesson that there are winners and there are losers. If your child gets really heartbroken when they lose, definitely get cooperative games before you get this one.

I would recommend this only for children starting at 5 years of age if you have spent time playing other board games, especially cooperative style board games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Sun Catchers Craft Kit I thought this would be a cool activity to do with my 6 year old. She LOVES crafts, and I actually bought a coloring "stained glass" art book by Klutz for her in the past (which she loved)
It was a little hard to tell exactly what the process was of making them just by looking at the pictures, and It was actually a bit more difficult than I assumed.

So you take the colored film paper, trace the shape out of the book, cut it out, then place it on the sticky paper to puzzle all the colored pieces together like a mosaic, to make up the whole picture. You youths choose to do them any color you want, but the more colors you use to make up the picture, the more patience and precision you will need.
We started off simple with the strawberry (only 2 colors) which was pretty easy.
I went to apply the puff paint and it would not come out of the top of the tube. I tried to cut the nozzle down, squeeze it out slow which ended in it coming out the side of the bottle, and getting all over my fingers. It was so thick, I assumed it got semi dried out, so I threw it away to prevent any further mess.
Since we were unable to use the puff paint, my daughter outlined the strawberry with black sharpie. Unfortunately without the puff paint, the film paper is pretty flimsy.
Even though we did not get the full effect of the project, we still had some fun doing the craft together.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Sun Catchers Craft Kit

text_fidelity_a:
BIC Magic Marker, Flexible Brush Tip (4.5 mm), Assorted Colors, Kids Coloring, 220-Count Bulk Pack For Kids This is an awesome set of really nice markers. Be aware that the dividers holding all of the different markers in separate containers is not actually attached to the bottom in any way, so your order will almost certainly arrive with the markers disorganized, as mine did. However, a bit of tape and a jellybean bounty to the children soon put that right.

The line is a good clean line and the tips seem resistant to fraying when mushed a little too hard by small hands. The color saturation is very rich and worked well on the notebooks that we keep for coloring.

The highlight of this set is that the markers are advertised as not drying out when exposed to the air when children leave the lids off. If you have small children, you'll know that "put the cap on it" is a constant and tiresome refrain, so for families or teachers, this is a huge and thoughtful benefit. While I didn't test keeping the lids off for 90 days, a couple of overnights assured me that for more normal, temporary times of the lids being off, the markers are not prone to drying out.

Overall this is a fantastic set for teachers or homeschoolers who go through more than the usual amount of art supplies. It would also be great for a party where coloring a themed item is part of the event.
text_fidelity_b: BIC Magic Marker, Flexible Brush Tip (4.5 mm), Assorted Colors, Kids Coloring, 220-Count Bulk Pack For Kids

Super excited in theory.. with ability to use manually or with electronic option as needed- it seemed ideal by just a flip of a switch on bottom. Only for some reason, pedal doesn’t respond every time like it should!! (Yes! battery is full when trying it- yet 15% of time it wont respond electronically- reason deducted x1 star!!?) When pedal engages- scooter is stable, easy to glide and maneuver.. and enjoyed. Battery outlasts our toddler whose rides for 15-25min straight and it hasn’t run out! (For reference: our little is 33mo, 36lb, 38” tall.. almost 3yr old.)

because of electronic component- ours struggles to grasp concept without using the pedal since he’s learned to ride with the electronic aid! So, when it fails to respond or we have pedal off- he just “jerks” scooter back/forth and side/side- its as if he’s trying to get it to do what it “should..” by tugging it into motion. For some reason.. he doesn’t naturally get moving scooter without electronic help so, it can leaves him fristrated.

Instructions are straightforward and connecting handle atop the scooter can be a tad tricky and tight.. Best if use included hardware to connect all screws loosely first THEN, tighten after all parts are aligned. Light up wheels are just extra!!! Not needed and not sure how long they’ll last esp. rider encountered water elements? I love the “long press” music feature- ha, it’s my fav. **bc, It shuts music all the way off!!

We’ve only used inside on tile and large smooth nape rug. No tire markings is nice.. I like inside option bc it’s winter here! I realize some issues had may be caused by our rider himself- but feel pedal should not be a problem we have to deal with if it’s charged. Hoping info can help decision.. stay safe everyone!

Playroom Entertainment Ascension Deckbuilding Game: Ascension Eternal The game itself is pretty fun. It's quick to learn for a strategy card game and fun to play. A good variety in cards means no two games are really ever going to be exactly the same. There really isn't anything bad I can think of to say about the game play itself, I've had nothing buy fun playing it and I have played it a lot. The art work is all very nice and fitting to the setting.

There were however some quality issues with my set. Four of the same card is misprinted with the wrong type written, which was quite confusing and took some time to figure out. When packaged, the cards are split into two slots in a tray for storage, and then plastic gems added in one of the two slots. The gems are very sharp and pokey, and there was so little room, the gems stabbed the top card a whole bunch, which makes it look very ugly and you can tell what card it is before it's even drawn. This could have been easily fixed by putting more cards in one slot, as there was plenty of room, and then the gems wouldn't have been pressed so hard into the cards they were with. Lastly, my game board was misglued, and looks really bad, and it's the side you play on of course. Though, it is still useable.

I still would recommend it though, I don't see anyone else mention the problems I have with my set, so I'm sure it'll be fine, and none of those problems prevent play. As I said above, it is very fun.
text_fidelity_b: Playroom Entertainment Ascension Deckbuilding Game: Ascension Eternal

Money Savvy Pig - Pink Money Savvy Pig offers a fun and effective way to teach kids about money and its many important uses. Parents devote very little time to the concept of financial management, in spite of its critical nature, often because they are not sure how best to approach the subject. Money Savvy Pig makes it easy to introduce youngsters to these important concepts.

How does Money Savvy Pig work as an educational device? The answer is simple. By including four different chambers with different labels- one for spend, one for save, one for donate, and one for invest- kids gain a sense of financial management and money allocation. They learn that money has uses that go far beyond ordinary spending. Kids under the age of seven are not ready to learn the specifics of these different concepts, but early exposure is a good idea and the Money Savvy Bank Pig certainly succeeds in this respect.

The Money Savvy Bank is made from plastic and mine has held up fine thus far. Others have pointed out that this bank can break if dropped on a hard surface. Considering its lightweight design, it isn't difficult to imagine the bank breaking apart if mishandled, which is why parents need to exercise caution and make sure their kids handle the bank with extra care when moving from one place to the next.

I like that this bank separates money into four different sections and I like that it gets kids thinking about money and its uses. One limitation, however, is that this bank isn't very good for storing paper money. The reason is because the pieces of paper are difficult to remove. The openings on the bottom of the bank are small- too small to stick your hand inside the bank to remove paper. Place a folded dollar bill inside this bank and it will take some shaking and maneuvering to remove it from the bottom. Thus, this bank should be avoided for storing paper currency. It is intended for use with coins.

Financial literacy is important and kids need to learn about money at the youngest age possible. The Money Savvy Pig is a very good piggy bank for youngsters and its benefits go far beyond the encouragement of savings. It encourages kids to ask questions and think about money in different ways, making it a great choice for a child's early financial education.
text_fidelity_b: Money Savvy Pig - Pink

Mecha Beasts Playing Cards by Gent Supply I have a few “collectible” decks of playing cards, this one among them. These are fancy cards that are made well and I like them, but the color scheme is a bit off for the black suit cards due to the background.

I’ll start with my main complaint with these first. These are dark cards, using a dark gray background for all suits, and using a dark purple for spades and clubs. This creates a low-contrast scheme that is more difficult to see in low light, and is less than pleasant even in brighter light. This is an unfortunate choice that could have been handled better. A bright purple, or even a strange color choice like orange or blue, would have worked better.

The artwork on these is impressive. A good bit of detail went into each design and it shows. The number cards (2 -10) have small designs on them that are at times hard to see and look at without a magnifying glass, though.

This are well made cards, coated and designed so they will not stick together even in damp climates. They come in a beautiful tuck box with reflective highlights in purple.

These are not bad cards at all. They’re beautiful and they’re well made, and they have some incredible artwork. However, the color scheme is not the best and these cards would be even better if the background and black suit colors were chosen a little more thoughtfully.

As a die hard Star Wars Fan this Saber has a lot going for it, but a few cons. First the build and look are nice. The sound is also very good. The price is one of the best reasons for getting one. As of today a 40% off coupon making it around $72.00. To me at this price point shows you how much Disney and Star Wars The Black Series is ripping people off.

For the $72.00 you're getting 12 Light Sabers "colors" compare that to $250.00 and higher for one color. Now for the cons the blade is held in place by three set screws and it still has a bit of a lose feeling not much but its there. The other thing is the control button it is a bit cumbersome and by that I mean the holding down or pushing or doing the fast twist while holding button down to change sound fonts. I know some other saber makers use similar features but not this hard to change. One of the sound fonts is not even from Star Wars. I did not know what it was and could not stand it, but you might like. The problem was it took me several tries to change it and it should not be that hard to change.

So even with those two minor faults, this is still a great Saber for the price. As someone who was 10 years old when Star Wars came out, even now holding this and turning it on makes me smile.

"May the Force be with You"

Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder This version adds difficulty without making it more interesting. In this game, there are both railways and ship routes to build, which means you have to collect cards for each route in the correct color and mode of transportation. Effectively, this game adds twice the number of colors you have to collect to build things. In the original game, you always end up with a bunch of cards in your hand that aren't useful to you because they're not the colors you need to finish your tickets. This game is twice as bad in that regard. Furthermore, there are fewer ship cards, even though you're expected to build more ship routes than train routes. Many of the ship cards are actually worth 2 of that color, which theoretically allows you to collect fewer cards of that color before building, but what actually happens is that you can go through the entire stack of ship cards without getting what you need because the other players are unintentionally hoarding the few cards in the color and type you need.

I didn't hate this game, but I wouldn't play it again.
text_fidelity_b: Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder

text_fidelity_a:
All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions [[VIDEOID:moOM6Q7TMDWRNW]]This is like an awesome mix between Apples to Apples and Trivial Pursuit. It's played very similarly to Apples to Apples, but you have an open-ended question, and everyone writes answers down on a piece of paper. Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

Pros:
+Awesome questions
+Fun game
+Good quality
+Well designed

Cons:
-You need 4 people to play according to the rules, even though these are fun questions to ask if there are just two or three of you
text_fidelity_b: All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions

text_fidelity_a:
Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover [[VIDEOID:bf921d7e8b73b1b75b44b485dab75323]] So after a week of having this unit I had 9 flights and was pleased to fly it! Although I had an issue once don't know if that was just the bird or that was me, I'm leaning toward me as I might have not turned the drone in the right direction and had a failure to calibrate or that could been just the area I was in and its inability to gain GPS, with that said it was pretty much a problem free week of flying the 270. Now dealing with the single battery was an issue, I do think they should offer a package or drone deal with 2 batteries standard. 😁.

I will say it is a great beginner drone for young teens are adults that want to get into flying. From the moment I unboxed it it felt great in my hands it didn't feel cheap most of the construction was plastic but with that said it is very consistent with some of the quality that I've become accustomed to with the hs700 the hs190 and a hs720. The controller is smaller then what I'm used to. It felt good in the hand but a lil small for my liking as I used my Galaxy Note 9 which is the limit as far as the holder, every other feature like the FPV, follow me mode and plotting way points , and circle point of interest on a map and it's going there and coming back worked pretty well. The Return too home when low on Battery functioned well as I flew the bird too that point almost everytime, there was an issue with the follow me I should have had it up a little higher it did hit a branch on a tree which was my fault because these drones do not come with obstacle avoidance and it took a fall to the ground no worse for wear I stopped the motors flipped back over unlock the motors and she went right back up no issues. Photo quality really really love the camera and take some great pictures even out that 400 ft. I really like the 4K camera and the quality of the video and pictures ( all photos post are unedited) and this unit also allows you to record record audio which is pretty good for bloggers , though my one gripe is I wish the 270 came with a gimbal to really make exceptional video, but at this price point it's a trade off!

The HS270 is very very wind resistant I flew this in pretty high winds somewhere between 15 to maybe 18 miles an hour and some strong gusts I thought for sure it going to blow over the pond or even into some of the trees. The GPS worked awesome as it kept the unit in its place and even though in my video it was shaky because you could see the wind is blowing it all over the place I was thoroughly impressed and this bird should not fly away from you unless you accidentally turn off the GPS in which case you really need to know how to fly this thing or any drones in the wind with the GPS off. It has a 3-speed future from low medium to high I enjoyed that it seemed like when it was windy I kicked it in high speed and it flew alot better keeping in medium most of the other times I enjoy a quick flights back and forth but was able to enjoy the roughly 21 minutes of flying time at the most and less on that really windy day it was only about 16 minutes most of the time it was fighting the wind. It takes pretty good pictures fpv to the cell phone like 720pvideo and 2K photo But the quality really comes to life when you have a SD card in the unit.

I think overall this unit does exactly as it's advertised to do and being able to fold up you can actually take this thing with you on vacation put in your suitcase carry out with you when you go on a hike and have something with you besides your camera that you can put up into the air and taking it up sectional a different view all of your vacation or a picture of you and your family or significant other standing by a Mountain or even the Grand Canyon with a drone from a distance and capture something that cant be done with a selfie stick. So I recommend this unit, but make sure you get extra batteries cuz it does take a while with the USB plug to charge the battery, most times it took 2-3 hours till fully charged. I grabbed a case on Amazon which I believe it was a case setup for a DJI mavic I did a little modifying on the sides of the hard foam and it was able to sit down in the case well which I showed the picture in the reviews it was the soyan case for like 22 bucks or something like that. All in all a great deal, I'm totally satisfied!
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice

text_fidelity_a:
Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog Sometimes when I get a box of Bloks, I chuck the instructions, dump them in with the rest of my collection, and make something cool with some of my favorite new pieces. I really liked the look of this one though, and I haven't followed the instructions for a while, so I actually built it to spec. I wasn't sure if there was any logic to all the separate and nested baggies, but half way through I concluded that the answer was "very little". I dumped them all in a dark colored jewelry display tray and things went much more smoothly. I definitely learned a few things about how some of the pieces can work together, and the end result came out looking nicer than most of the pre-built toys out there these days, but fully customizable. There are quite a lot of Bloks left over after completing the main instructions, and they've included some suggested modifications with build instructions, like the missile launcher in one of the pictures.

There were some minor flaws. The windshield doesn't attach very solidly. The two dudes are so burly and heavily armored that they don't fit inside gracefully. A few of the pieces shrunk just enough when they cooled that they ripple a bit differently than the things they are supposed to look smooth with. Lastly, while the instructions are very good, this set is mostly different shades of black and dark silver, which weren't adequately differentiated in the pictures which made locating the right parts in the heap difficult

The build process, with its sorting and instruction struck me as.something that would be a good project to do with my 3 year old son, since he is developing all the needed skills right now. Maybe instead of a puzzle, we'll build a warthog together on the next rainy day.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog

text_fidelity_a:
Dimension - A 3D Fast-Paced Puzzle Game from Kosmos | Up to 4 Players, for Fans of Strategy, Quick-Thinking & Logic | Parents' Choice Silver Honor & Oppenheim Toy Portfolio Platinum Award Winner Though it can at times feel a bit simple, overall Dimension is a fun game that plays quickly and makes for fast, easy to learn family fun.

Packaging and materials: everything in its place, easily held in place, all in good shape, no excessive packaging, easy to open and easy to store back in the box. The balls have a good sense of heft to them, stack easily in their spots, and are well-made. Our son dropped a good number of them the first few times playing and after the first few, our nervousness about the balls breaking or chipping disappeared (though we still wished he’d control their rolls a bit better . . . ) Cards are also well-made, as our the playing boards--heavy stock that come with stick-on feet to hold them slightly off the table surface so the balls don’t move around too easily. All in all, construction is a plus.

Directions: For the most part, directions are quite clear and are pretty minimal. The directions also offer up a few variant forms of the game for making things easier or more challenging, though to be honest, anyone could have come up with those pretty easily and quickly (for instance, upping the number of challenges one has to meet)

Game play.
You each take some point markers to start, and place your 15 spheres--five trios of different colors-- in your game board (again, the balls rest solidly in their holes).

The center of the game board is where you will build patterns with the balls depending on the card challenges. There are seven spaces in the building area, and you can build upward from those spaces, employing up to three layers and up to 11 spheres (7 in your bottom layer, three in the middle layer, and one on top).

You lay out six cards, each one detailing a particular challenge you must meet when you build your patterns. Some examples:
Two specific colors must touch (i.e. somewhere in your pattern, a blue sphere must contact a white sphere
Two specific colors must not touch
You must use a specific number of a particular color
One color must outnumber another (i.e. you must have more green spheres than white spheres)
Two colors must total a specific number (i.e. between blue and white spheres, you must total 4: 1 blue and 3 white, 2 and 2, 1 white and 3 blue)
A particular color cannot be laid atop any of the other colors
A particular color cannot have any of the other colors put on top of it (i.e. your green spheres must be the topmost layer)

once the cards are laid out, you turn over a one-minute timer and try and create a 3-dimensional pattern/pyramid that will meet as many of the challenges as possible.

You get one point for each challenge you meet and lose two points for each one you miss. There is a bonus for meeting all six and/or using all the colors. You also get more points the more spheres you use, though you’ll have to weigh quickly whether adding more spheres to get more points might break a rule and thus lose more than you gain (for instance, adding another blue sphere would get you a point, but if in doing so you broke a rule by having it touch a green sphere, you would lose two points).

As you can see, sometimes the rules may conflict (you might, for instance, get a card that says blue and white must touch and another that says blue and white cannot touch). In those cases, each player decides for him/herself which challenge they choose to ignore.

An entire game is six rounds and most points wins.

It goes very quickly and as you might guess, the speed and difficulty of each round is determined by the combination of cards. Sometimes all three of us were done well before the timer, other times we were all caught with spheres still in our hands trying to figure out where to add or remove a color. And sometimes you’d smoothly and confidently total up your six points for meeting all the challenges and other times as you were oh so cockily adding another challenge to your list you’d suddenly realize, “Doh--how did I end up with a green touching a blue?!”

Mostly the game moves along quickly and the combinations are decently challenging, though we all thought we’d probably move on to doing 8 challenges soon to up the difficulty even more. The only other point I’d make is an electronic timer would be nice as you’re all concentrating so hard on your pyramid that we’d often miss the time running out, or you’d just pluck off a ball to replace with another when someone noticed it was done and you were stuck. We’ve therefore actually taken to using one of our iPhones as a timer to give us a 10-second beep before the full time runs out.

The other nice thing about the game is it is pretty easily modified for playing to younger levels--dump the timer, drop a color, uses only three or four cards. The game can grow with your kids. Certainly even 5-8 year olds can play simpler versions and then grow into more difficult challenges. Fun to play, a bit different, uses some different skills. Recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Dimension - A 3D Fast-Paced Puzzle Game from Kosmos | Up to 4 Players, for Fans of Strategy, Quick-Thinking & Logic | Parents' Choice Silver Honor & Oppenheim Toy Portfolio Platinum Award Winner

Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab Fisher-Price Imaginext toys in general are great toys. Durable, bright colored plastic that often take after popular shows and movies such as Batman and Superman, Power Rangers, or in this case, Jurassic World. These toys have allowed my son's imagination to run wild and be creative as he plays for many hours with these. We often play together, but for the most part he's very happy to play with these on his own for hours at a time. I probably purchased my first Imaginext toy about 3 years ago, Batman and his Batcycle. It has held up to the test of time and a very rough preschooler. My son is now 6 with multiple sets.

Jurassic World has been all the rage in my house this summer because little boys love dinosaurs and that is certainly true of mine! So, take his love for Imaginext toys and mix that with his love for dinos and it's the perfect mashup! The only caveat is that on Amazon I have found the prices to vary greatly from in stores. Toys R Us (R.I.P.) was a great source for Imaginext because they always had the best and lowest price on these. They also had more selections. So, I would caution anyone to first look around Target or Walmart first. I once bought Batgirl and her Batcopter for $30 on Amazon and it was in Toys R Us for $15. I regularly see Imaginext toys in Target selling for $5-10 cheaper than on Amazon.

With the Fisher Price Imaginext Jurassic World Research Lab you get one T-Rex, one scientist, one harpoon, and one claw. There is a "decontamination" chamber for the scientist to get clean to study his subject. Simply turn the powerpad and the blue decontamination spiral gets the scientist ready. There is a powerpad to open and close the cage for the T-Rex. But watch out! The T-Rex might get loose! the lab is not that big. It's smaller than all of the Batcaves I've ever purchased. It's no bigger than any of the Paw Patrol sets I've purchased as well. So, it's east to tuck it away in a corner. All of the pieces, including the T-Rex, we've placed in a plastic show box for organization and storage. Overall, it's a fun play-set that provides hours of entertainment and keeps kids away from screens!

text_fidelity_a:
Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Short version of the review: it’s a fun game with a pretty good first-game learning curve that settles in pretty quickly in subsequent games. It can be long (though you can adjust it). We’ll add it to our rotation of “lengthy” games

Longer version

1) Packing
I’m going to ding the game for packaging because while everything comes fine (as is typical, there’s a lot of popping pieces out of their cardboard sheets), I like when games include easy ways of keeping thing together and/or organized once you’ve played the first game. Even if it’s as minimal as separate small plastic bags. We used our own tiny bags (we’ve learned to keep ones that do come with other games if they’re extra thanks to consolidation) and a few regular small baggies, but I don’t think it’s too much to ask that those things be included

2) Materials
All the materials seem of good quality. Cards are not super-thick but they’re not at all flimsy, the non-plastic pieces feel solid and you don’t have any sense that they’ll start coming apart or getting dented/torn. The plastic cities are a nice touch, but the capital cities could perhaps have been made a little more distinctive. Not at all a big deal; a close look is all you need.

3) Instructions
The big sheet of instructions is fine. Generally clear and well written, with a few “clarification” points at the end, which is a nice touch. We had a few questions that weren’t included, but they were easy to find online. A few individual player cards with a stripped down bit of instruction for quick, easy reference would have been nice to toss in

4) Set up
As noted (and as is usual for these types of games) there’s a lot of popping things out and organizing. Once that’s done the first time, set-up is relatively quick. You put together some map tiles which is easy enough (though this 50+-year-old wouldn’t have minded if the organizing numbers were a little bigger on each tile). Each player gets tokens, a set of cards five of which are laid out in a particular order under their “Focus” bar (the cards are in these areas: Military, Technology, Culture, Economy, Industry), a set of “diplomacy” cards, a “leader” card (who they “play”—Cleopatra for instance), a few caravans (little wagons used for trading). After you’ve done it a few times it’s a pretty quick set-up. You also set up some cards to the side of the play area (World Wonder cards and City-State Diplomacy Cards and Victory Cards (these are what determine how the game is won). This is always an issue in these sorts of game because of course they’re not going to be truly “visible” to all the players. Someone is going to have to move or ask to see them to see what they say (some change throughout the game). I have no idea how to get around that though; it’s just a matter of physical setting.

5) game play
I’m not going to detail it. But generally, the Victory cards have two “agendas” on them, such as build two Wonders of the World, and a player who achieves one agenda from each of the cards is the winner (this is nice because you can shorten the game if desired by simply playing with fewer Victory cards). As far as the play itself
1) Players can “resolve” (do what it says) any one of the five cards below their Focus bar. This might mean building a city, attacking someone, moving a caravan, laying out a “Control” piece to claim a hex space (i.e. territory).
2) Once they’ve done that, that card gets move to slot one under the bar and all the others move one slot to the right. This is key because the slot number affects how the card is resolved. For instance, when you attack using your military card, you roll a die and add the slot number (and possibly other bonuses) to your roll. So you’re going to want to attack when that card is in the 4 or 5 position typically, not the 1 or 2 slot. This adds a nice bit of complexity to your action choices.

That’s pretty much the gameplay for players. A few other factor include
1) You can swap out a card under your focus by advancing your “Tech” counter a certain number (you do that using one of the cards). Once you hit a certain level, you can exchange one low level card for one that’s a bit more powerful. There are 4 levels of cards.
2) Barbarian tokens on the board move at regular periods and they can end up destroying one of your caravans or claiming territory from you (which affects how much money your cities earn and how much you can advance)
3) Caravans allow you to gain trade tokens that can be used to increase the impact of your cards. For example, if you have two trade tokens on your military card, you can spend one or both to add a bonus to your roll. Caravans can also garner you another player’s Diplomacy card, which has certain benefits dependent on the card.
4) Placing a control tokens mean you’ve claimed territory (that particular space), which is necessary for collecting trade tokens (a “mature” city garners you a set number of trade tokens once you’ve “controlled” all adjacent tiles), collecting resources such as marble or diamonds, or for building cities (your build cities a certain number of spaces from a space you’ve controlled with a token).
5) The terrain has an impact on your choices. In order of scaled “easiness”, the terrains are 1-grasslands, 2-hills, 3-forest, 4-desert, and 5-mountains. To travel through a desert is considered difficult, so that 4 means your Economy card (the one that moves your caravan) needs to be in the 4 or 5 slot. Similary, to build a city in a mountain space means your Industry card has to be in the 5 slot.

There are more rules and factors that come into play, but that’s the general gist. As noted at the start, I’d say the learning curve is relatively steep the first time ( a lot of going back to the instruction booklet), but past the first game or two, it comes pretty easily. I’ve certainly played games with a far steeper curve and one that takes longer to get to know game play well. If I were ranking learning curves on a ten-point scale, I’d probably put this around a 6.

Turns move slowly the first time or two as people try to remember what they can do, what they need to do, etc. But after the first hour each player moves pretty quickly through their turns as you’ve gotten used to how to deal with the complexities of those shifting slots under the Focus bar. As people get closer to each other, things slow again as players try and figure out cost-benefit of attacking, but then as before, after a few attacks those move quickly.

I liked the game quite a bit. More than my two family members, but I tend to have more patience for the slowness of things and I mind long game less than they do. They did like it enough to play again. And as mentioned, I like that you can self-adjust your length simply by cutting out one of the agendas. It’s a game we’ll definitely keep and keep playing.
text_fidelity_b: Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a:
Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.
text_fidelity_b: Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea

LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink Mix feelings about this product. Had it over a year with minimal travel usage. We usually leave it in our dining room on our kids table so they can do activities while mom cooks. We loved it when it worked but once the batteries died and I replaced the device with new batteries, it turns on and does nothing. It doesn't sense the stylus. It will on a random occasion after multiple attempts say one or two words when pointed on the stylus but then stops again. Changed batteries out a couple of times and unfortunately didn't help. Now, I have two disappointed kids with numerous of these books and told family to get more books for Christmas which will only be to their disappointment that they have no device to use them with.

As for when the device worked, we would loved it and would recommend to any parent with kids under 7. My son is almost 5yo son and 3yo daughter love this. They take turns using it since I only had one of the Leap Start devices but numerous books. My daughter was heart broken after multiple attempts to try new batteries.

I hate to give one start but given the longevity of this product for the price, it needs to last more than a year. I mean one year for a $45 device. Maybe some would say that's worth it but not when you shell out $10 - $15 on each of the books. I might of gotten a faulty device so maybe it's just poor luck on my part.

Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3) This is one cool Mickey! In fact, he's so cool his "ice cream doesn't melt"! (one of his cheesy phrases, not mine) Seriously, this has to be one of the coolest toys ever. Not only do both of my boys(16 months and 3 3/4 years) like it, but my husband and I love him, too. Whenever we have visitors, we have to pull this Mickey out, just to show him off. Sad, but true. One day, my 11 year old nephew was over here, and he even commented that this is the "coolest Mickey ever", and his little brother has the original dancing Mickey. I'm not familiar with the other dancing Mickeys, but apparently this one has more features.

My only complaint is the batteries, which really can't be helped with the kind of toy it is. This is more of simply a warning for you than a complaint. This Mickey really sucks the power out of batteries! He takes 6 AA batteries. He does come with a set, but they will wear off REALLY quickly. I would definitely have a high quality set of batteries waiting nearby. When the batteries get low, he will keep moving, but he won't be able to do the really fancy moves, like the handstand, and leg spins. Those are my favorite, so it's disappointing when I don't get to see those. ;)

To make him dance, all you have to do is press his nose. He will only do one set of dance moves and then he will tell you if you want to see more, just press his nose. He turns off pretty quickly. I'm sure this is so he won't use up the batteries even quicker. I like that he's smart, too. When he falls over, he asks for help getting up. When you help him up, he says, Thanks, pal!". There is an on/off switch on the back of his head. I have to make use of this switch when my youngest takes a nap.

Overall, if you don't mind the big investment price and the many batteries he will require, we HIGHLY recommend this Mickey!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3)

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer (My 1st 2-in-1 Wagon, Red Is this easy to assemble? Apparently! My 3 little guys put it together while I was cooking supper. So, it's also quick to assemble. They did a great job, minus putting the handle on backwards. Though I've tried to take the wheels off to move the handle around, I've been unsuccessful. That hasn't kept them from having a great time with it, though. My older 2 have pulled my 3 year old around in it, and he has had a great time loading and unloading his stuffed animals. The good news is, even if put on backwards, the handle still locks!

This wagon is on the small side. My 3 year old is small for his age, but he still has to squeeze in there. I wouldn't recommend older than that riding in it due to fearing it will break. It also flips over pretty easily, so I don't recommend too much riding in it, period, especially for the younger little ones. It IS great for pulling things like stuffed animals and books around, though.

This wagon is plastic, like most of the other Radio Flyer toys these days. We have a few of them, and they have always been well loved and played with by my boys. Despite being plastic, they have proved to be very sturdy so far.

Overall, you really can't go wrong if this wagon is for pulling little toys around. It will provide hours of (semi)quiet fun for your little one. If you're wanting something to pull a child around in, though, I'd go a different route.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer (My 1st 2-in-1 Wagon, Red

text_fidelity_a: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone Our family loves word games, and I was hoping this would be one we could add to our favorites. The idea is similar to other games out there - (first thing I think of is Scattergories) - where you have to quickly think of words that start with a specific letter for a particular category. In this case, the category might be "pizza toppings," and then you call out an item, tapping down the letter it starts with, and hand it off to another person who has to call out another item starting with another (non-tapped) letter, etc etc, until the timer buzzes. The concept is generally ok. But there are better versions of this type of game out there. More creative, I guess. And I honestly do NOT like the design of the Tapple board that gets handed around. It's nearly impossible to quickly pass it off without accidentally tapping down one of the letters in the process. Big design flaw. We *have* found an unexpected use for this game - it's been a fun way to help my 6yo expand his vocabulary. We don't play the game, per se, but do use it without the timer and have him think up different words within each category. But for a group game? I'll pass.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is just one of dozens and dozens of slime toys intended to fascinate the young scientist in your home. The way most of these labs works is similar: Combine the included slime mix, if any exists, with a few household items like baking soda, vinegar, cornstarch, etc., and let the fun begin.

This slime toy works like the others in terms of the mixing, but it is also different than others, and I mean that in a good way. With this slime lab, the mixture is placed atop a motor that vibrates for greater effect. Kids can watch the colors and textures swirl around as the vibrations create some fun and very visual patterns. The instructions include 20 different recipes for slime and each can be made using items found in most kitchens.

What I probably like best about this slime lab is the lack of mess! Okay, there is some mess but in relative terms, the messiness is kept under control very well. The key difference is that, with most other slime labs my kids have used, messiness is encouraged. These other labs involve sticking hands in the slime, spreading it with your hands, and so on. This is messy and gross, and if multiple kids are involved, they often end up smearing it on each other, splattering it on the floors and more. There is no problem like that with SmartLab. The slime, for the most part, stays in the bowl, out of your way.

Educational toys are nice and SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is a toy that does get kids thinking and asking questions. My girls like it and have returned to it more than once, creating more slime and learning about household chemicals and how they react. It’s a good choice of toy that will keep kids entertained as they learn.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab
